title: Idle time has no definition, and turn_end means two different things
foundBy: the user, who asked how the tool should account for time and set the rule that an agent stopping with no tool call is waiting; the checks that followed found the adapters disagreeing
details:
Nothing in the schema or the spec says what idle time is, and no adapter reports it. A reader wanting to know how long an agent sat waiting has to subtract timestamps, and the viewer would have to guess which gaps count.

The guess is not available either, because `turn_end` does not mean one thing. Claude and codex emit it once to five times per trajectory, at a real boundary. OpenCode emits it for every `step-finish`, which fires after each batch of tool calls. In a captured corpus that is 892 events across twelve trajectories, 31% of every strip, against three real endings per trajectory. Only the step whose reason reads `stop` ends a turn.

Telling them apart today means matching the word `tool-calls` inside the event text. R65 forbids exactly that, and the fixture scrubber rewrites text to prose, so the corpus could not exercise it.

The cost is not academic. The interval after a real turn ending holds most of the elapsed time. It measured 97.9% in one captured session, and 88% and 55% in aggregate for the two unattended adapters. A tool that cannot name that interval cannot say how long anything took.

A `step-finish` that is not a turn ending is bookkeeping, and it belongs in `meta` with its reason preserved, where the details page still shows what it was.

To reproduce, normalize an opencode session and count the `turn_end` events against the turns the session actually contains.
